plan_title: Scout Energy Management, LLC Rangely Field Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The boundary of the Rangely Field (Rangely Weber Sand Unit) plus a one-half mile buffer, since free-phase CO2 is already present throughout the field and is retained by pressure and lease-line fluid management (p19-20).
mma_definition: Same as the AMA: the Rangely Field Unit boundary plus the required one-half mile buffer, because the plume is expected to stay within the unit (p20).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Existing wellbores and pipeline/surface equipment are treated as the only meaningful pathways; faults/fractures, natural and induced seismicity, previous operations, lateral migration, future drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated very low risk (p21-26).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The baseline is ongoing operational data captured by existing automatic data systems: visual inspection work orders, personal H2S monitor alarms, SCADA injection rate/pressure set points, and production volume/composition forecasts used to flag excursions (p30-31).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report (filed by March 31) with the mass balance and estimated surface leakage; records retained at least three years; well failures and MIT results reported in parallel to COGCC and equipment leaks under Subpart W. No commitment to publish measurement data (p25-26, p29, p35-37).

rows.detail: Custody transfer meter on CO2 received from the Raven Ridge pipeline; operations meters at the inlet and outlet of the CO2 reinjection facility; composition sampled at least quarterly; meters NIST traceable, API standards.
rows.location: Raven Ridge pipeline custody transfer point; CO2 Reinjection Facility inlet and outlet

rows.detail: WAG manifold flow meters and pressure monitors feed SCADA, which compares each injector to its weekly pattern plan and flags deviations from high/low set points; satellites have automatic shutoff if pressure exceeds fracture pressure.
rows.location: Each injection well (WAG manifold) and injection satellites
rows.trigger_or_response: Pressure or rate outside set points: field personnel investigate; unresolved issues get a work order and detailed investigation; screened for leakage.
rows.evidence_quote: Well pressure in injection wells is monitored on a continual basis.

rows.detail: Annular pressure in wellheads monitored, with changes in tubing and annulus pressure used to detect tubing and casing leaks; annular leakage detection devices mentioned as part of well procedures.
rows.trigger_or_response: Anomaly: field personnel inspect and repair; well shut in and workover crews respond within days.
rows.evidence_quote: monitoring of the annular pressure in wellheads

rows.detail: MITs under COGCC rules before injection, every five years, after casing repair and whenever tubing or packer is reset; casing-tubing annulus tested to 1,200 psi for 15 minutes with COGCC witness.
rows.trigger_or_response: Failed MIT: well shut in immediately, COGCC notified, leak repaired and retested or well plugged.
rows.evidence_quote: Every 5 years as stated in the injection orders (COGCC 417.a. (1))

rows.detail: Each producer tested at its collection station about twice per month (roughly 24 hours) for oil, water and gas rates; produced gas composition sampled at least quarterly; sales oil sampled annually for CO2; performance compared to forecast.
rows.location: 382 production wells via 27 collection stations; RCF inlet; oil LACT
rows.trigger_or_response: Significant deviation from forecast: well management investigates; work order if unresolved; leakage quantified if found.
rows.evidence_quote: Most wells are tested twice per month.

rows.detail: Bottom-hole pressure surveys across the field one to two times per year, with designated monitor wells (Appendix 5) used to watch reservoir pressure against the ~3,730 psi induced-seismicity threshold; also listed in the response table for faults, spill points and seismic events.
rows.location: Monitor wells across the Rangely Field (listed in Appendix 5)
rows.trigger_or_response: Reservoir pressure above ~3,730 psi: reduce nearby injection; shut in injectors near faults or seismic events; reseal abandoned wells if high pressure found.
rows.evidence_quote: bottom hole pressure surveys are collected one (1) to two (2) times per year across the Rangely Field

rows.detail: Routine two-part visual inspection of wells and surface facilities by about 25 field personnel, looking for white CO2 clouds, ice, fluid line leaks, valve leaks and WAG schedule compliance; also watches for unapproved drilling.
rows.location: Field-wide wells, pipelines and surface facilities
rows.trigger_or_response: Leak or problem found: repair on the spot or generate work order; critical leaks acted on immediately; volume quantified for reporting.
rows.evidence_quote: field inspections are conducted on a routine basis by field personnel.

rows.detail: All field personnel wear H2S monitors at all times (10 ppm detection limit); H2S treated as a proxy for CO2 leaks, including diffuse leakage through the seal.
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, verify monitor, investigate source; confirmed H2S incidents reported to MRV lead; not used to determine leak volume.
rows.evidence_quote: all field personnel are required to wear H2S monitors at all times.

rows.detail: Cement bond logs and pressure tests named as examples of corrosion-protection procedures in COGCC injection orders; not tied to this plan's monitoring.
rows.evidence_quote: procedures (e.g. packer placement, use of annular leakage detection devices, cement bond logs, pressure tests)

rows.detail: Historical USGS seismic stations (1969-1973) and a USGS earthquake catalog map (1900-2023) are discussed; induced seismicity is managed through reservoir pressure, with no ongoing seismic monitoring commitment.
rows.trigger_or_response: Response table: shut in injectors near a seismic event.
rows.evidence_quote: Between 1969 and 1973, a joint investigation with the USGS installed seismic monitoring stations in and around the town of Rangely

rows.detail: Existing 3D seismic reinterpreted to identify joint faults near the main field fault; characterization only, no repeat survey.
rows.evidence_quote: A new interpretation from the 3D seismic revealed a series of previously unknown joint faults

rows.detail: Subpart W emission factors and engineering estimates used to quantify equipment leaks and vents between meters and wellheads and any other surface leak; work orders track events for reporting.
rows.evidence_quote: SEM uses 40 CFR Part 98 Subpart W to estimate surface leaks from equipment at the Rangely Field.

rows.detail: Reservoir pressure management by holding injection-to-withdrawal ratio near 1.0, lease-line well operation and pattern modeling that sets injection targets below historic step-rate fracture pressure; cited as containment and seal-protection measures.
rows.trigger_or_response: Unexplained injection pressure changes trigger investigation; fluid management along lease lines if overfill beyond spill points.
rows.evidence_quote: Reservoir pressure in the Rangely Field is managed by maintaining an injection to withdrawal ratio (IWR) of approximately 1.0.

notes: No image-only pages; figures are referenced but their content is not in the text. Appendix 5 (p43-67) is a well list in which 'Monitor' status means a well used for bottom-hole reservoir pressure; these are the monitor wells referenced in Table 3 but the plan never states their number or survey instruments. Reservoir pressure surveys are '1 to 2 times per year'; coded as annual (the weaker reading). Production well tests are 'twice per month'; coded as monthly with the actual cadence in detail. Table 3 lists 'high pressure found in new wells' as a monitoring method although SEM has drilled no new wells. The plan cites a Section 2.2.3 and Figures 11/12 that do not exist. 'Pressure transducers with low pressure alarms' on surface equipment (p24) are pressure sensors, not gas detectors, so fixed_gas_detectors is not_found. The response table lists 'Loss of bottom-hole pressure control' with 'blowout during well operations' as the monitoring entry, which is not a monitoring method.
